newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: UN official tallies Cambodia human rights problems.
newsitem.headline: UN official tallies Cambodia human rights problems.

text.p: Cambodia's human rights problems range from a chaotic judicial system and political violence to a lack of laws protecting labour, U.N. rights official Thomas Hammarberg said on Friday.
Hammarberg, special representative of the U.N. Secretary-General for Human Rights in Cambodia, made the comments at the close of a two-week mission here.
"I don't think it is alarmist to say the situation is fragile," he told reporters.

Hammarberg said the judicial system was of particular concern. He said courts were poorly equipped, judges were ill-trained, officials were granted impunity from their crimes and judges and prosecutors were threatened.
Hammarberg also cited violence against party activists and journalists, and called conditions in some garment factories appalling.

During his visit, a local U.N. Human Rights Day celebration fell apart over political infighting, Human Rights Watch/Asia declared 1996 the worst year for Cambodian human rights since national elections in 1993, and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen questioned the wisdom of funding some rights groups.

Hun Sen and First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh have been increasingly at odds over reported political intimidation, and Ranariddh said last week he did not think national elections, scheduled for 1998, would be free and fair.
"I have observed a climate of nervousness," said Hammarberg when asked about the situation for human rights workers.
He emphasised Cambodia's need for continued international aid to protect rights with the approach of elections, expressing concern that funding might dry up.
A local rights worker told Reuters: "If the donor countries withdraw, that will kill human rights here."
